comparison.verdict: Clean-holdout F1 with rehearsal+EWC changed by +0.0017 (worst -0.0745, 1 verdict flips); without it, -0.0017 (worst -0.0759, 1 verdict flips). Mean absolute probability shift on the same holdout was 0.0046 protected vs 0.0040 unprotected. Caveat on resolution: the two arms differ by 0.0034 F1 on a holdout of 600 URLs, which is a handful of individual verdicts. The sign of that gap is not established by this run and must not be quoted as evidence either way. The protected arm ended with no clean-set F1 loss. Whether that is the protection working or the ceiling simply not moving is the question the caveat above leaves open. On the adaptation side the difference is real: stream F1 finished at 0.9981 protected vs 0.9516 unprotected (from 0.8664 after the first round). Rehearsal plus EWC therefore bought adaptation, not immunity: the protection measurably improved how well the model handled the newly observed URLs while leaving the forgetting question above unanswered.

honesty_note: Every number here is measured in this run. Negative final_change means the metric is worse than the shipped model. No arm's results were selected post hoc; when the protection failed to help, the verdict string says so.
